items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-CFN-26-005, 2026 Grant Report
notes:
This report was pulled from the consent agenda.

Committee expressed interest in the Region supporting a greater variety of organizations, in terms of both organization size and amount of resources they operate with.

In response to questions from Committee, Commissioner Planning, Development & Legislative Services, Rod Regier, provided rationale as to why one million dollars was the threshold in the policy framework. During review of the policy framework staff marked a minimum revenue of one million dollars as a way to designate what organizations can be considered as key cultural institutions. This benchmark is a way for an organization to demonstrate its robustness and ability to serve the community sustainably. 

Committee also inquired into K-W Oktoberfest and the Child and Youth Planning Table and how the funding application process works for youth organizations. Committee would like further information on how funds are distributed and the decision framework.

Committee also raised the importance of equitable geographic representation in terms of both grant criteria and advisory committee membership. Staff did confirm that the Grant Policy framework is set to be under review and will come back with a report to the next term of Council. Staff also committed to circulating more background information on the request by the City of Kitchener Museum.

In response to a question by Committee, R. Regier explained the role of the Empty Space organization. Empty Space functions as an administrative body that provides services on behalf of the Region, this is the third year that they have been awarded with a grant for its programming and services. Empty Space also functions as a theatre company.

Committee also expressed interest in receiving data on how money has been sent to organizations in each municipality. Committee also noted that a report will be coming in the near future on bringing back a Regional Arts committee.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-CFN-26-004, 2025 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results
notes:
Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications, Connie MacDonald and Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, Wayne Steffler, provided a presentation. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda.

In response to questions from Committee, W. Steffler explained that tax write offs are budgeted for, this means that staff take data from MPAC and forecast out what the expected tax write offs are for the year. If the number comes in lower than expected it means the number of write offs is down.

Committee also inquired into capital expenditures and the use rate. 2025 ended with a 51% use rate of the capital budget, Committee inquired into how the percentage of budget use can be stable and consistent. Staff explained that there is an internal staff committee that explored how the Region can best allocate funds to capital projects; supply chain delays have led to some of the underspend.

W. Steffler. explained to Committee that municipalities have other mechanisms that they can use to gain back tax revenue that is not paid if citizens are in arrears, tax sales are the main alternative. Municipalities are not required to pay out of pocket if someone is in arrears.

Committee also inquired into the Police Services Budget and how some line items are over budget. Staff committed to coming back to Committee with additional information on the line items in question.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-CFN-26-002, 2026 Tax Ratios and Capping Program
notes:
W. Steffler provided an introduction to the report.

In response to questions from Committee, W. Steffler addressed the idea of a vacant home tax and why staff are not in favour of enforcing it. Staff have determined that the amount of vacant homes in the Region and the time required to enforce the tax would not make it the tax worth while.

Committee inquired further into the possibility of adjusting the ratios as presented, staff confirmed that adjustments to these ratios can be made at a later time.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-26-004, 2025 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2025 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results as set out in report COR-CFN-26-004 dated April 7, 2026: Receive the 2025 Plan Update that shows implementation and progress toward achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care Strategic Plan 2023-2027; Approve the preliminary 2025 financial results for the purposes of preparing the Region’s 2025 Audited Financial Statements; and Amend the Surplus Allocation Policy and apply such amended Surplus Allocation Policy to the 2025 financial results.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2025 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results as set out in report COR-CFN-26-004 dated April 7, 2026:

  1. Receive the 2025 Plan Update that shows implementation and progress toward achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care Strategic Plan 2023-2027;
  2. Approve the preliminary 2025 financial results for the purposes of preparing the Region’s 2025 Audited Financial Statements; and
  3. Amend the Surplus Allocation Policy and apply such amended Surplus Allocation Policy to the 2025 financial results.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-26-002, 2026 Tax Ratios and Capping Program
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2026 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-26-002 dated April 7, 2026: Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2026 property tax year: Residential and New Multi-residential 1.000000 Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial 1.950000 Aggregate Extraction 1.586727 Landfill 1.540000 Pipeline 1.161300 Farmland and Managed Forest 0.250000 Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2026 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2026 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 22, 2026; and Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2026 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-26-002 dated April 7, 2026:

  1. Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2026 property tax year:

    • Residential and New Multi-residential 1.000000

    • Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial 1.950000

    • Aggregate Extraction  1.586727

    • Landfill 1.540000

    • Pipeline 1.161300

    • Farmland and Managed Forest 0.250000

  2. Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2026 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2026 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 22, 2026; and
  3. Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.
